body:
Behavior is not replicated with the demo project on Windows 11 (24H2) same setup - AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti SUPER.
I'm thinking it's probably some artifact of the way input is handled on MacOS.

Validated on `v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]` with latest macOS.

It's worth noting that this happens with some other apps on macOS. For example, if I have Messages or Music (built-in macOS apps) unfocused and I click on one of their elements (e.g. a song record in Music or a conversation in Messages) then the window is focused but not the element. However if I double click then it is as if the window was already focused and the element was double-clicked. Notably, the built-in sidebar widget (used in Music, Finder and other apps) does not exhibit this behaviour, so it may be configurable by the application, seemingly on the widget level.

Not sure if it's particularly worth checking other versions for this behaviour as a result, and it seems to be standard on the platform so I am unsure if it is strictly a 'bug' actually. It may be a less ideal behaviour for Godot as a game engine, so there could be some merit in seeing if we can disable it, but this would make it inconsistent with other software on the platform which could also not be ideal. Potentially it could be worth having a setting easily exposed to control this behaviour on macOS if that's possible so it could be controlled by the developer.

```
Godot v4.4.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.5.0) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M1 - Apple M1 (8 threads)
```

I can confirm, the "click on unfocused" window behaviour in macOS is not consistent across applications. For example, the already mentioned default music app (while not focused) forwards a double-click event (= starts playing), but not a single click (= would normally select) on a music item. Many other apps seem to just not handle the first click at all...

To have a more baseline point for reference on macOS, I've created a minimal native app via Xcode/SwiftUI to see how that behaves. In the video you can see, that each click is translated into a button action, independent of window's focused state:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e58e49d-f77b-405f-8b6b-1d7abb0032d5

I'd still label this issue here as a bug. I think the way Godot is handling double-clicks on unfocused windows is broken in one detail. Godot issues `Button.pressed` **twice in quick succession** even for **slow double-clicks**, when the double-click started on an unfocused window. There is a very noticable delay between the first real-world click and the first reported `Button.pressed` happening.

Refining my proposed options for resolving this issue:
- Option A: emit `Button.pressed` as soon as they really happen, i.e., also the first click on the unfocused window
- Option B: only emit `Button.pressed` for the click(s) that happen after the window has focus ("consume first click")

@svn133 I'm not convinced this is a bug in Godot still, given this can be replicated in various native first-party macOS applications there's an argument this is standard behaviour in the platform. Any slow/fast double click I performed in Godot I could replicate in Music with identical behaviour. My guess, though I haven't verified it, is macOS is deciding whether to pass the event to Godot or not, probably based on the double click speed defined in your system settings. There seems to be some way to configure this behaviour since it isn't universal, which should potentially be surfaced by Godot, but that would be an enhancement rather than a bug.

@CreatedBySeb I agree, looks very much like system behaviour, from what I can see. I had a look into Godot's mouse event handling for macOS (`godot_content_view.mm`) and could not find any suspiciously looking delaying functionality. So probably really something off with NSView's dispatching of events.

But I found something interesting, that might resolve this issue in favor of "Option B" ("consume first click"):
- Return `NO` in the `acceptsFirstMouse` function in `godot_content_view.mm`.
- That would explicitly disable event dispatch of the "first click" and resolve this issue.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b22b41531c82132732fda0f9818c5709c2587bc/platform/macos/godot_content_view.mm#L69-L73

see https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nsview/acceptsfirstmouse(for:).
